items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: pay by pounds of butterfat by the test at the station where he delivered, not by weight of milk.
Story 1: 'Under payment by weight, the glass would have cost nobody anything.'
Only Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) appears; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill never named.
Son of Gideon stated, but manager 'from 1911' (Stories 4, 6), a planted error; key requires 1913.
Story 6: yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account', more fat arriving than credited.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Stories 1-2: milk weighed, sampled, tested; fixed 17.6 c.c. charge read on ruled neck; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; 1898 rejected.
Story 2: full invoice lines, 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Story 4: deficit 0.19, 'the same in every month, flush and winter alike' ('flat as a floor').
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that there was none in the county.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924 (Story 1); dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 7).
Test book kept by Ansel from 1896 and used against him (Stories 1, 5); the bolded gate is the test book.
No summary leaf; 1896 average of 3.80 never given, only the 3.61 long-run average.
Dates 8 May-10 July and question mark given, but tests only 'markedly higher', explicitly unquantified; no 3.80.
Story 3: married to Orra, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron; irony stated.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent; both elements required.
Died February 1934 with the charge never withdrawn; test book impounded, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Story 3: six farms, Emmet's the largest.
Story 3: weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 (Duncan's date accepted); scales always agreed.
Story 4: first complaint 1902; 3.61 vs 3.78 kept apart from the 0.19 deficit against true 3.80.
Story 4: Jan-Mar 1908 committee (Grigg's sleigh) blamed wet bog hay; reported as its finding and then refuted.
Story 3: 200,000 lb at 3.42, true 3.60 via 0.95; Story 2: error reads low 'by exactly the same proportion'.
Story 3: to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962.
Only 'Jerome Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners' 'over the ridge'; Redlow Ridge and Vessey County as its location not given.
Four patrons in summer flush stated, but no 1915 start.
Independence of the Alder Corners test not argued; fewer than two of the four elements.
Only 'tested normally there'; no 0.19 higher, no sixteen overlapping seasons.
Draws only 'never the cows'; describes the milk as going to the two places in different months; hay/watering not disposed of by this comparison.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, copied/sent the Alder Corners figures to Ivy (Stories 4, 8).
No 1907-1936 span; asserts lactometer visits 'from 1908 on' (NT-23 planted error).
Story 4: lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
Story 7: 12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Says only he 'drew no inference about the years before'; never states he wrote no figure for the deficiency or made no report beyond the condemnation.
Asserts 'From 1924 the station tested 3.85' (planted error); key requires 3.80.
Crate to the loft (Story 7); notebooks to the state office in 1936 and the college library in 1947 (Story 8).
Story 7: petition January 1925.
Board 17 March-4 May 1925, two of three sittings in the weigh room; chair unnamed ('an Ashlin attorney'), but the core fact is present.
Only the theft theory is placed at the hearing; three explanations argued and none accepted not stated.
Story 7: four books incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody set it beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 'no cause established'; $3,800 'without admission' charged to station account.
One-fifth of $19,000 stated, but not that the award was charged to the very account where the loss had accumulated as 'gain'.
Story 8: Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student, State Agricultural College, Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Her gathering of records is described, but 'records never in the same room' is not stated in Section A (the scattered-record idea appears only in G).
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes (eleven rejected).
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 5%.
Proportional 5% short reading, 3.61 for 3.80, 0.19 short, 0.95 ratio across Stories 2-4, 6.
Story 6: 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at $0.25, identified with the ledger's station-gain difference.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; cleared 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter; Duncan is Ansel's son.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Declares full vs half undeterminable but says a half-sibling link would make them 'half second cousins'; never states it does not change the answer (a bolded requirement).
Gideon Vose, father.
Father's Article 7 turned the short pipette into a cut in pay; the son signed the water circular.
Asserts 'On the evidence there was no kinship'; E row 17 'No relation'. Assertion.
Treats the family denial as outweighing hearsay rather than saying no document names or denies a link.
0.95, 95% of true, 5% low.
$90 at 25c, explicitly stated as the long-run average price with working shown; accepted per key.
5.26% of credited and 5.00% of received, both denominators named.
$77.93 with the sum shown.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
26 years and 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898-1922; part years 1897 and 1923 excluded.
Cannot be determined; Kyle's figure is hearsay. Correct abstention.
Variable: the measuring glass, station's own vs borrowed.
Tester, herds, pasture, feed, season, acid, scales held constant.
Only 'rose markedly' and 'fell back'; no 3.80 during the interval, no 3.61 on return.
Establishes the cause is in the glass, not water, theft or hay; limits: which piece, size of error.
Ledger (Kyle), 1911 (Falke/Orra/Duncan), 1924 rise (Falke), Alder Corners (Hazel): three or more narrators.
Independence argued; ledger, 1924 rise and Alder Corners named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'no, the bookkeeper never questioned the ledger entries'.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low (1902 complaints, 1919 circular).
Only two valid: signed ledger sheets and wrote the 1919 circular. Manager dated 1911 (wrong); watering at the hearing and 'never names the glass' are absent.

Headline 'cannot be shown' counts as an abstention (no deduction), but none of the five required observations is given (it relies on Kyle's claim that he read only totals, not the signature-vs-reading point).

Weigh book 1897 over 1900 (Hazel disclaims years); Orra b.1866 from 'eighty-two in 1948'; 1908 committee and 1925 board as distinct bodies. Capped at 3. (Circular resolved wrongly to eleven; Strawn/Vose/1924 rows missed or wrong.)

NT-14 $77.39 pair (Junia and Chronicle) broken by the invoice total and line sum; NT-18 great-niece pair (Chronicle and Falke) broken by Falke's correction and Duncan. No other pair identified as a pair.
A04 (knowing vs accidental short lot): cannot be determined, works books burned 1931. A06 not addressed as a conflict; A10 abstained only in Section A, which is out of scope for E.
r20's 'nothing before 1900' vs her own 1897 invoice; r18's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'.
72 pipettes at 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, 0.19 = 5% of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897, cessation 12 June 1923, nothing on farms changed. (3.85 for 1924 penalized via deduction.)
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus (more fat arrived than credited).
Bog hay (1908 committee) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter-only effect vs a flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: the tester believed the cause 'was in the glass'.
About 134 words.
Names the ledger and the 1958 measurement explicitly; the invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, notebooks, minutes and by-laws are not named as records. Fewer than five.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure (3.61/3.80/76,000/$19,000/$3,800).
5% short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted (Stories 4, 6; B3; D3)
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer visits/circuit from 1908 asserted (Story 4; F2)
Corruption: 1924 station average 3.85 asserted (Story 7; D2; F1)
Corruption: water circular sent to eleven families adopted (Story 4; E row 12)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved 'no kinship' (B4; E row 17)
Gullibility A09: 'no, the bookkeeper never questioned the ledger entries' (D2)
Gullibility A05: tester believed the cause was in the glass (F)
